title: Run of the tape trimming machine
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $i$ be one of $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $\mathrm{words}$ assign a Boolean word to each work tape. Starting with the machine in its forward-pass state on input $x$ and with these words on the tapes, after exactly $2|\mathrm{words}(i)|+2$ steps it is in its completed state, with tape $i$ replaced by the word obtained by removing its trailing $1$s and every other tape unchanged. It does not enter that completed state at any earlier time.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is a work-tape index among the $k$ tapes
$\mathrm{words}$ assigns a Boolean word to each work tape
The run begins in the forward-pass state with the specified tape words
At every time strictly less than that run length, the state is not the completed state
